name: CUPID-0
summary: CUPID-0 was a scintillating-bolometer demonstrator at Gran Sasso searching for selenium-82 neutrinoless double-beta decay. It demonstrated particle identification with crystals developed through LUCIFER.
detection_principle: Enriched ZnSe crystals measure heat, and thin germanium light detectors measure scintillation. Combined pulse-shape and light-to-heat selections reject alpha backgrounds around the decay energy.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The final dataset provided a selenium-82 neutrinoless-decay limit and demonstrated the scintillating-bolometer method.

results.summary: The final dataset provided a selenium-82 neutrinoless-decay limit and demonstrated the scintillating-bolometer method.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
